description: This dashboard displays metrics from a DCGM Exporter on a Kubernetes cluster.

panels.description: Hotspot temperature from gpu-vram-temps (gputemps); nvidia-smi does not show it. Red = alert threshold (88 C).
panels.title: GPU 0 Junction

panels.description: GDDR6X memory (incl. back-side chips) temperature from gpu-vram-temps (gputemps); nvidia-smi does not show it. Red = alert threshold (92 C).
panels.title: GPU 0 VRAM

panels.description: Hotspot temperature from gpu-vram-temps (gputemps); nvidia-smi does not show it. Red = alert threshold (88 C).
panels.title: GPU 1 Junction

panels.description: GDDR6X memory (incl. back-side chips) temperature from gpu-vram-temps (gputemps); nvidia-smi does not show it. Red = alert threshold (92 C).
panels.title: GPU 1 VRAM

panels.description: Fan % (left) against VRAM and junction temperature (right). 'curve target' is what gpu-fan-curve set; a gap in it means the driver is in control (idle / cool).
panels.title: GPU 0: fan vs VRAM

panels.description: Fan % (left) against VRAM and junction temperature (right). 'curve target' is what gpu-fan-curve set; a gap in it means the driver is in control (idle / cool).
panels.title: GPU 1: fan vs VRAM

panels.description: Hotspot and GDDR6X memory temperature, from gpu-vram-temps.timer on the host. dcgm-exporter ships a 15-field default counter set that excludes DCGM_FI_DEV_MEMORY_TEMP, so this cannot come from DCGM. GDDR6X throttles at 110C and runs far hotter than the core - this panel replaces Tensor Core Utilization, which needed DCGM_FI_PROF_* profiling metrics that are not exposed either.
panels.title: GPU Junction / VRAM Temperature

title: Better NVIDIA DCGM Dashboard
